title: Solo dev, no art skills: how I went from 53 to 400 AI illustrations for my iOS life sim
author: LifeStartsToday
selftext:
I'm a solo dev from Korea, and this is my first game, Life Starts Today. It's a life sim where you start with your paycheck and try to survive month by month. Every event gives you a few choices, and each one changes your money, health and stress. There's also a fictional stock market if you feel like gambling your savings.

I can't draw, so every event illustration was made with AI (GPT image generation), and I used ChatGPT heavily for planning and for the Unity code. I started with 53 illustrations for the first batch of events and slowly worked up to around 400, one for each event, so the picture matches what the player is actually deciding. Keeping 400 images feeling like the same game was a bigger job than generating them.

The hardest part wasn't the art though. Localization into 5 languages (Korean, English, Japanese, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, each with its own currency) took way more effort than I expected, because event text that fits nicely in Korean often overflows the card in English. And as a non-designer, getting Unity UI right was painful. Card spacing, where the choice buttons sit, and making it all fit different iPhone and iPad screens took several updates. I also don't own a Mac, so every iOS build went through Unity Cloud Build from Windows.

For those of you making games with AI art: how do you keep a consistent style once you're past a few hundred images? And has anyone found a good AI workflow for localization that doesn't need a native speaker to fix everything afterward?

App Store (free, with ads): https://apps.apple.com/us/app/life-starts-today/id6816805326
